Great find — that fully explains it. Here's the exact ERB from `kamal_ssh_block/0` in deploy_artifacts.ex, verbatim:

<% if ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>
ssh:
  keys: ["<%= ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>"]
  keys_only: true
  log_level: debug
<% end %>

Note: in a fresh cms-new project this whole `ssh:` key only exists when the env var is set — there's no separate always-present `ssh:` block to merge into, because the generator never had one before this. Your files already have `ssh:\n  user: root` unconditionally, so don't duplicate the top-level `ssh:` key (two `ssh:` mappings in one YAML file is asking for it to silently pick one). Nest the conditional inside your existing block instead, so `user: root` always applies and the rest only applies once CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH is set:

ssh:
  user: root
  <% if ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>
  keys: ["<%= ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>"]
  keys_only: true
  log_level: debug
  <% end %>

Do that in both config/deploy.yml and config/deploy.uat.yml (indentation matters — keep the ERB tags at the same indent level as the keys they're gating, kamal's YAML+ERB parser is picky about it). Once that's in, your next deploy attempt should actually get `keys_only: true` wired up and stop falling back to password.

Worth surfacing to John separately: this is a real generator gap — `generate_deploy_files` never patches an existing hand-written kamal config with newer template pieces, so any pre-cms-new project is permanently missing fixes like this one unless someone finds and manually backports them, like you just did. # Kamal config for cleaner_crm UAT on the Hetzner UAT box (Nuremberg ARM).
# Run with: scripts/deploy-uat
#
# Same shape as deploy.yml; differs in host, and arch. Service name
# matches deploy.yml so the multi-arch image labels resolve.

service: cleaner-crm
image: code-my-spec/cleaner_crm

servers:
  web:
    hosts:
      - 46.225.105.88
    options:
      network: db_net           # pre-attach so app can reach infra-postgres-1 at start
    proxy:                      # role-level override
      ssl: true
      host: uat.maidfor.cleaning
      app_port: 4000
      healthcheck:
        path: /                 # app has no /up; / is 200 for the localhost probe

registry:
  server: ghcr.io
  username: johns10
  password:
    - KAMAL_REGISTRY_PASSWORD

builder:
  arch: arm64
  local: true

# Container fetches its own secrets from /cleaner_crm/uat/* in SSM at
# boot via CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!/1 (config/runtime.exs). The only env
# Kamal carries is AWS bootstrap creds + APP_ENV.
env:
  clear:
    APP_ENV: uat
    AWS_REGION: us-east-1
    PORT: "4000"
  secret:
    - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

ssh:
  user: root

#!/bin/sh
# Release overlay: turn the age key into an environment, then start the app.
#
# Setup encrypts each environment's secrets into `envs/<env>.enc.env` and
# commits the ciphertext, and hands the container exactly one secret —
# SOPS_AGE_KEY, that environment's own private key. Per-environment keys
# mean UAT's cannot open production's, so being able to deploy UAT
# discloses nothing about production.
set -eu

cd -P -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.."

ENV_NAME="${APP_ENV:-prod}"
ENV_FILE="envs/${ENV_NAME}.enc.env"

if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  echo "$0: no $ENV_FILE in this image — setup encrypts one per environment" >&2
  echo "$0: APP_ENV=$ENV_NAME; the image holds: $(ls envs 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "${SOPS_AGE_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "$0: SOPS_AGE_KEY is not set, so $ENV_FILE cannot be decrypted" >&2
  echo "$0: the deploy carries it to the host — see config/deploy*.yml env.secret" >&2
  exit 1
fi

exec sops exec-env "$ENV_FILE" "./bin/cleaner_crm start"

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

# === Secret loading ==========================================================
#
# Deployed containers (UAT + prod, both MIX_ENV=prod) carry only AWS
# bootstrap creds + APP_ENV; every app secret is fetched from SSM
# Parameter Store (/cleaner_crm/<APP_ENV>/*) into System env here,
# BEFORE any config below reads it. Local dev/test never set APP_ENV.
if config_env() == :prod do
  case System.get_env("APP_ENV") do
    nil -> :ok
    app_env -> CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!(app_env)
  end
end

content.text:
Traced it fully, and this is genuinely reassuring — here's the mechanism:

`config/runtime.exs` shows `CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!(app_env)` runs **unconditionally** for any prod release with `APP_ENV` set (both uat and prod always set it), and per its own comment: it fetches every app secret from AWS SSM (`/cleaner_crm/<APP_ENV>/*`) "into System env here, **before any config below reads it**" — including `DATABASE_URL`, read a few lines later via a plain `System.get_env("DATABASE_URL")`.

That means: even though `bin/boot` decrypts code_my_spec's own `envs/uat.enc.env` first (which does contain the fresh `app_cleaner_crm_uat` connection string), `Secrets.load!/1` runs immediately after and **overwrites** `DATABASE_URL` from whatever's actually in AWS SSM. So the app's real database connection is controlled entirely by SSM, not by code_my_spec's managed secrets — the fresh database it minted is currently inert/unused by this app. As long as nothing touched that SSM parameter (nothing tonight did — no tool I've used has AWS access), the legacy data should still be exactly what the live app connects to once it actually boots.

One thing I can't do myself: my local AWS CLI session has expired (`aws sts get-caller-identity` fails), and I don't have another sanctioned way to query SSM through this harness (`provider_request` only covers Hetzner/Cloudflare/Resend). If you can refresh it (`! aws sso login` or whatever your normal auth flow is), I can pull the actual `/cleaner_crm/uat/DATABASE_URL` value directly and confirm this with certainty instead of architectural inference.

I think that structurally protects the legacy infra-postgres-1 data from this deploy, but I can't verify SSM's actual current value myself (my local AWS session expired) — waiting on him to refresh it. Just flagging in case it's relevant to how you're thinking about the registry step too.

Found it, and I need to correct my earlier advice — sorry, that one was wrong for this topology.

Checked the box directly: `cms-registry` is up, healthy, but Docker published it as `10.1.0.2:5000->5000/tcp` — bound only to the private network interface, NOT loopback. Confirmed: `curl 127.0.0.1:5000` on that box itself gets connection refused; `curl 10.1.0.2:5000` gets a 401 (reachable, registry answering normally).

This is deliberate, not a misconfig — `serve_one_registry/5` in steps.ex explicitly does `Keyword.put_new(:bind, ip)` where `ip` is the box's own private network IP, with a comment explaining why: on a shared account server, the registry needs to be reachable by other boxes on the private network (builders, or other projects' servers), and Hetzner's private IP is the only address that's actually meaningful for that. It only falls back to loopback for the local-fleet test double, which has no private network at all.

So `registry.server` in your kamal config should be `10.1.0.2:5000`, not `localhost:5000` — that generic default only holds for a project with its own dedicated (non-shared) box, which fuellytics isn't. Same correction applies to `image:` — still bare `cleaner-crm`, that part was right, kamal will build `10.1.0.2:5000/cleaner-crm` itself.

Caveat worth knowing: `10.1.0.2` is the box's *current* private IP, looked up dynamically by code_my_spec's own provisioning each time it needs it — your static YAML will go stale if this box is ever recreated or its network re-attached. Not something to solve tonight, just flagging it as a real fragility in hand-editing this value into a committed file, since account-server plumbing normally isn't something a project's own config is supposed to know about at all.

Got the SSM/DATABASE_URL note too — that's for John, no action needed from me there right now.
</cross-session-message>

file.content:
# Kamal config for cleaner_crm UAT on the Hetzner UAT box (Nuremberg ARM).
# Run with: scripts/deploy-uat
#
# Same shape as deploy.yml; differs in host, and arch. Service name
# matches deploy.yml so the multi-arch image labels resolve.

service: cleaner-crm
image: cleaner-crm

servers:
  web:
    hosts:
      - 46.225.105.88
    options:
      network: db_net           # pre-attach so app can reach infra-postgres-1 at start
    proxy:                      # role-level override
      ssl: true
      host: uat.maidfor.cleaning
      app_port: 4000
      healthcheck:
        path: /                 # app has no /up; / is 200 for the localhost probe

registry:
  server: 10.1.0.2:5000
  username:
    - KAMAL_REGISTRY_USERNAME
  password:
    - KAMAL_REGISTRY_PASSWORD

builder:
  arch: arm64
  local: true

# Container fetches its own secrets from /cleaner_crm/uat/* in SSM at
# boot via CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!/1 (config/runtime.exs). The only env
# Kamal carries is AWS bootstrap creds + APP_ENV.
env:
  clear:
    APP_ENV: uat
    AWS_REGION: us-east-1
    PORT: "4000"
  secret:
    - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

ssh:
  user: root
  <% if ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>
  keys: ["<%= ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>"]
  keys_only: true
  log_level: debug
  <% end %>

# Kamal config for cleaner_crm PROD on the Hetzner prod box (Ashburn x86).
# Run with: scripts/deploy
#
# NOTE: no prod DNS/host exists yet — UAT (config/deploy.uat.yml) is the
# live environment. Update `proxy.host` before the first prod deploy.
#
# Notes:
# - kamal-proxy serves traffic on :80/:443 directly.
# - db_net is pre-attached so the container can reach infra-postgres-1 at start.
# - App secrets are fetched at container boot from AWS SSM
#   (`/cleaner_crm/prod/*`) by CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!/1 in
#   config/runtime.exs. Kamal carries only the AWS bootstrap credentials
#   listed under env.secret below — never app secrets.

service: cleaner-crm
image: cleaner-crm

servers:
  web:
    hosts:
      - 178.156.143.212
    options:
      network: db_net

proxy:
  ssl: true
  host: maidfor.cleaning
  app_port: 4000

registry:
  server: 10.1.0.2:5000
  username:
    - KAMAL_REGISTRY_USERNAME
  password:
    - KAMAL_REGISTRY_PASSWORD

builder:
  arch: amd64
  local: true

env:
  clear:
    APP_ENV: prod
    AWS_REGION: us-east-1
    PORT: "4000"
  secret:
    - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

ssh:
  user: root
  <% if ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>
  keys: ["<%= ENV["CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH"] %>"]
  keys_only: true
  log_level: debug
  <% end %>

defmodule CleanerCrm.Secrets do
  @moduledoc """
  Boot-time secret loader. Pulls every parameter under
  `/cleaner_crm/<APP_ENV>/` from AWS SSM Parameter Store and writes it
  into the OS environment so the rest of `config/runtime.exs` (which
  reads `System.get_env/1`) sees the values as if they were set in the
  container's launch env.

  Invoked from the top of `config/runtime.exs` in `:prod` when
  `APP_ENV` is set (UAT and prod boxes — both compile with
  `MIX_ENV=prod`). Local dev/test never call this.

  Kamal carries only AWS bootstrap credentials
  (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` for the per-env IAM user
  `cleaner-crm-<env>-app`) — app secrets never flow through the
  operator's shell or Kamal. See the devops repo's `infra.md`.

  The IAM principal needs `ssm:GetParametersByPath` on
  `arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:889081505590:parameter/cleaner_crm/<env>/*`
  and `kms:Decrypt` on the default `aws/ssm` key.
  """

  @path_prefix "/cleaner_crm/"

  # The typical failure is a transient network blip during a box-wide
  # restart, not SSM throttling — fixed backoff, few attempts.
  @max_attempts 3
  @backoff_ms 1000

  @doc """
  Load all parameters for `app_env` ("prod" | "uat") into System env.
  Raises on missing IAM creds, an empty parameter path, or any SSM
  error after #{@max_attempts} attempts.
  """
  @spec load!(String.t()) :: :ok
  def load!(app_env) when app_env in ["prod", "uat"] do
    # These ship with the release as regular deps, but nothing has
    # started them yet when runtime.exs runs. Req (not hackney) is the
    # HTTP client — hackney 4.x in this app's tree is incompatible with
    # ExAws's default client.
    {:ok, _} = Application.ensure_all_started(:ex_aws)
    {:ok, _} = Application.ensure_all_started(:req)
    Application.put_env(:ex_aws, :http_client, CleanerCrm.Secrets.ReqClient)

    path = @path_prefix <> app_env <> "/"
    parameters = fetch_all(path, nil, [])

    if parameters == [] do
      raise """
      No SSM parameters found under #{path}.
      Verify AWS credentials and that the path has parameters.
      """
    end

    Enum.each(parameters, fn %{"Name" => name, "Value" => value} ->
      key = String.replace_prefix(name, path, "")
      System.put_env(key, value)
    end)

    :ok
  end

  def load!(other),
    do: raise(ArgumentError, "CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!/1: unsupported APP_ENV #{inspect(other)}")

  defp fetch_all(path, next_token, acc) do
    case fetch_page(path, next_token) do
      {:ok, %{"Parameters" => params, "NextToken" => token}} when is_binary(token) ->
        fetch_all(path, token, [params | acc])

      {:ok, %{"Parameters" => params}} ->
        Enum.reverse([params | acc]) |> List.flatten()
    end
  end

  defp fetch_page(path, next_token, attempt \\ 1) do
    opts = [recursive: true, with_decryption: true]
    opts = if next_token, do: Keyword.put(opts, :next_token, next_token), else: opts

    case ExAws.SSM.get_parameters_by_path(path, opts) |> ExAws.request() do
      {:ok, page} ->
        {:ok, page}

      {:error, _reason} when attempt < @max_attempts ->
        # `reason` can carry AWS auth diagnostics — log only bounded fields.
        :logger.warning(
          "CleanerCrm.Secrets: SSM fetch failed for #{path} (attempt #{attempt}/#{@max_attempts}); retrying in #{@backoff_ms}ms"
        )

        Process.sleep(@backoff_ms)
        fetch_page(path, next_token, attempt + 1)

      {:error, reason} ->
        raise """
        CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!/1: SSM fetch failed for #{path} after \
        #{@max_attempts} attempts: #{inspect(reason)}
        """
    end
  end
end

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

# === Secret loading ==========================================================
#
# Deployed containers (UAT + prod, both MIX_ENV=prod) carry only AWS
# bootstrap creds + APP_ENV; every app secret is fetched from SSM
# Parameter Store (/cleaner_crm/<APP_ENV>/*) into System env here,
# BEFORE any config below reads it. Local dev/test never set APP_ENV.
if config_env() == :prod do
  case System.get_env("APP_ENV") do
    nil -> :ok
    app_env -> CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!(app_env)
  end
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

# Stripe credentials — see .code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md. Only
# CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live (never the test adapter) reads these.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
  secret_key: System.get_env("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
  webhook_secret: System.get_env("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET")

# STRIPE_ADAPTER=test swaps in the no-network fake gateway — for UAT
# until real Stripe test keys are seeded. Anything else keeps the
# compile-time default (Live in prod, Test in dev — see config files).
if System.get_env("STRIPE_ADAPTER") == "test" do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
    adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test
end

# Stripe *publishable* key — safe to ship to the browser, unlike the
# secret/webhook config above. Only prod ever sets it (already seeded
# in SSM on UAT); dev/test leave it unconfigured (`nil`), which is how
# `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Accept` decides whether to mount real
# Stripe Elements or fall back to today's hidden test-card field.
if config_env() == :prod do
  config :cleaner_crm, :stripe_publishable_key, System.get_env("STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY")
end

# Twilio — SMS delivery per the sms-delivery ADR. Unconditional (like
# the Stripe block above), not `:prod`-only: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.
# Delivery.Twilio` must always have *some* config to read. Missing
# credentials in dev/CI aren't an error here — `Twilio.send_sms/2`
# returns `{:error, :not_configured}` and the caller falls back to
# email, it never reaches the network or raises.
twilio_host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "localhost:4100"

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio,
  account_sid: System.get_env("TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"),
  auth_token: System.get_env("TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"),
  from_number: System.get_env("TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER"),
  status_callback_url: "https://#{twilio_host}/webhooks/twilio"

if config_env() == :prod do
  # Encrypted-token vault key — required in production.
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Vault,
    ciphers: [
      default:
        {Cloak.Ciphers.AES.GCM,
         tag: "AES.GCM.V1",
         key:
           Base.decode64!(
             System.get_env("CLOAK_KEY") ||
               raise("environment variable CLOAK_KEY is missing (base64 32-byte key)")
           )}
    ]
end

if config_env() == :prod do
  database_url =
    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
      raise """
      environment variable DATABASE_URL is missing.
      For example: ecto://USER:PASS@HOST/DATABASE
      """

  maybe_ipv6 = if System.get_env("ECTO_IPV6") in ~w(true 1), do: [:inet6], else: []

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
    # ssl: true,
    url: database_url,
    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10"),
    # For machines with several cores, consider starting multiple pools of `pool_size`
    # pool_count: 4,
    socket_options: maybe_ipv6

  # The secret key base is used to sign/encrypt cookies and other secrets.
  # A default value is used in config/dev.exs and config/test.exs but you
  # want to use a different value for prod and you most likely don't want
  # to check this value into version control, so we use an environment
  # variable instead.
  secret_key_base =
    System.get_env("SECRET_KEY_BASE") ||
      raise """
      environment variable SECRET_KEY_BASE is missing.
      You can generate one by calling: mix phx.gen.secret
      """

  host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "example.com"

  config :cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query, System.get_env("DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY")

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
    url: [host: host, port: 443, scheme: "https"],
    http: [
      # Enable IPv6 and bind on all interfaces.
      # Set it to  {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1} for local network only access.
      # See the documentation on https://bandit.hexdocs.pm/Bandit.html#t:options/0
      # for details about using IPv6 vs IPv4 and loopback vs public addresses.
      ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
    ],
    secret_key_base: secret_key_base

  # Resend for real email delivery (fleet ADR). Only when the key is
  # present — a UAT/prod box without it keeps the Local adapter and
  # boots fine, emails just stay undelivered.
  if resend_api_key = System.get_env("RESEND_API_KEY") do
    config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer,
      adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Resend,
      api_key: resend_api_key

    config :cleaner_crm,
           :mailer_from,

  # and clients may not be supported. You can set it to
  # `:compatible` for wider support.

  # `:keyfile` and `:certfile` expect an absolute path to the key

cd /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Migrate off AWS SSM secrets onto the managed SOPS convention

CleanerCrm.Secrets.load!/1 (AWS SSM Parameter Store) was a pre-managed-
stack artifact and is exactly what broke tonight's uat deploy: the
container's AWS bootstrap credential was invalid, and the app crashed
on every boot before ever binding the health route. Since this project
now has a working sops-encrypted envs/<env>.enc.env + bin/boot decrypt
path (the standard cms-new convention), there's no reason to keep a
second, AWS-dependent secrets mechanism running in parallel.

- Removed CleanerCrm.Secrets and its ReqClient/test, and the runtime.exs
  call site — every secret was already read via plain System.get_env,
  so bin/boot's sops-decrypted env vars are a drop-in replacement.
- Dropped ex_aws/ex_aws_ssm (only ever used by the removed module).
- .kamal/secrets-common and both deploy configs: replaced the AWS
  bootstrap credential (env.secret + env.clear AWS_REGION) with
  SOPS_AGE_KEY, matching how the registry credential and CMS_SSH_KEY_PATH
  already flow through.
- Migrated the real values (Stripe, Resend, Cloak, SECRET_KEY_BASE,
  DATABASE_URL confirmed pointing at the legacy infra-postgres-1 data,
  not a fresh managed database) from SSM into envs/uat.enc.env, updating
  PHX_HOST/MAILER_FROM_* for the maidfor.cleaning rebrand.
- uat's healthcheck now probes the real /health route instead of the
  old "app has no /up" workaround pointing at "/".

Also picks up the previously-uncommitted health route, HealthController,
and cms_gen.support_widget output from earlier tonight — the build
clearly reads the live working tree directly (uncommitted changes and
all, since builder.local: true), so these were never blocking, but
they belong in history regardless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01P919w92byuTzie8N9tDBci
EOF
)"

# Dockerfile for the Cleaner CRM Phoenix app.
# Multi-arch: built by GitHub Actions for linux/amd64 (prod box) and
# linux/arm64 (Hetzner cax11 UAT box). Same two-stage shape as the other
# apps in the fleet (see the devops repo).

ARG ELIXIR_VERSION=1.19.4
ARG OTP_VERSION=28.1
ARG DEBIAN_VERSION=bookworm-20260223-slim

ARG BUILDER_IMAGE="hexpm/elixir:${ELIXIR_VERSION}-erlang-${OTP_VERSION}-debian-${DEBIAN_VERSION}"
ARG RUNNER_IMAGE="debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}"

# ---- Build stage ----
FROM ${BUILDER_IMAGE} AS builder

RUN apt-get update -y && apt-get install -y build-essential git curl nodejs npm \
    && apt-get clean && rm -f /var/lib/apt/lists/*_*

WORKDIR /app

RUN mix local.hex --force && mix local.rebar --force

ENV MIX_ENV="prod"

# Install mix dependencies
COPY mix.exs mix.lock ./
RUN mix deps.get --only $MIX_ENV
RUN mkdir config
COPY config/config.exs config/${MIX_ENV}.exs config/
RUN mix deps.compile

# Copy all application code
COPY priv priv
COPY lib lib
COPY assets assets

# Copy runtime config and release overlays
COPY config/runtime.exs config/
COPY rel rel

# Install npm dependencies (html-to-image for the feedback widget)
RUN cd assets && npm ci && cd ..

# Compile and build assets (tailwind/esbuild binaries via hex packages)
RUN mix assets.setup
RUN mix compile
RUN mix assets.deploy

# Build release
RUN mix release

# ---- Runner stage ----
FROM ${RUNNER_IMAGE}

RUN apt-get update -y && \
    apt-get install -y libstdc++6 openssl libncurses6 locales ca-certificates curl \
    && apt-get clean && rm -f /var/lib/apt/lists/*_*

RUN sed -i '/en_US.UTF-8/s/^# //g' /etc/locale.gen && locale-gen

ENV LANG=en_US.UTF-8
ENV LANGUAGE=en_US:en
ENV LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8

WORKDIR "/app"
RUN chown nobody /app

ENV MIX_ENV="prod"

COPY --from=builder --chown=nobody:root /app/_build/${MIX_ENV}/rel/cleaner_crm ./

USER nobody

CMD ["/app/bin/server"]

# Dockerfile for the Cleaner CRM Phoenix app.
# Multi-arch: built by GitHub Actions for linux/amd64 (prod box) and
# linux/arm64 (Hetzner cax11 UAT box). Same two-stage shape as the other
# apps in the fleet (see the devops repo).

ARG ELIXIR_VERSION=1.19.4
ARG OTP_VERSION=28.1
ARG DEBIAN_VERSION=bookworm-20260223-slim

ARG BUILDER_IMAGE="hexpm/elixir:${ELIXIR_VERSION}-erlang-${OTP_VERSION}-debian-${DEBIAN_VERSION}"
ARG RUNNER_IMAGE="debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}"

# ---- Build stage ----
FROM ${BUILDER_IMAGE} AS builder

RUN apt-get update -y && apt-get install -y build-essential git curl nodejs npm \
    && apt-get clean && rm -f /var/lib/apt/lists/*_*

WORKDIR /app

RUN mix local.hex --force && mix local.rebar --force

ENV MIX_ENV="prod"

# Install mix dependencies
COPY mix.exs mix.lock ./
RUN mix deps.get --only $MIX_ENV
RUN mkdir config
COPY config/config.exs config/${MIX_ENV}.exs config/
RUN mix deps.compile

# Copy all application code
COPY priv priv
COPY lib lib
COPY assets assets

# Copy runtime config and release overlays
COPY config/runtime.exs config/
COPY rel rel

# Install npm dependencies (html-to-image for the feedback widget)
RUN cd assets && npm ci && cd ..

# Compile and build assets (tailwind/esbuild binaries via hex packages)
RUN mix assets.setup
RUN mix compile
RUN mix assets.deploy

# Build release
RUN mix release

# ---- Runner stage ----
FROM ${RUNNER_IMAGE}

RUN apt-get update -y && \
    apt-get install -y libstdc++6 openssl libncurses6 locales ca-certificates curl \
    && apt-get clean && rm -f /var/lib/apt/lists/*_*

RUN sed -i '/en_US.UTF-8/s/^# //g' /etc/locale.gen && locale-gen

ENV LANG=en_US.UTF-8
ENV LANGUAGE=en_US:en
ENV LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8

WORKDIR "/app"
RUN chown nobody /app

ENV MIX_ENV="prod"
ENV PHX_SERVER="true"

COPY --from=builder --chown=nobody:root /app/_build/${MIX_ENV}/rel/cleaner_crm ./

USER nobody

CMD ["/app/bin/boot"]
